title: Iroquois Beaver Wars
summary: In the 1600s the Haudenosaunee (Six Nations) fought wars across the Great Lakes and Ohio Valley, and later used them to claim rights over Kentucky.
bodyMarkdown:
In the 1600s the Haudenosaunee, or Five (later Six) Nations, fought a long series of wars against neighboring peoples, often called the Beaver Wars, for control of the fur trade. The fighting reached across the Great Lakes and into the Ohio Valley.

Historian A. Gwynn Henderson notes that early written references to peoples in the Bluegrass and middle Ohio Valley are mostly secondhand reports, and that some groups had already moved or merged with others before Europeans arrived. Disease spread along trade routes and reduced populations in the region.

By the 1700s the Iroquois "wanted to control the Ohio Valley," Henderson writes, and they asserted rights over it as conquerors. The Shawnee, who claimed much of Kentucky and lived and hunted there, disputed that. In 1768 at Fort Stanwix the Six Nations sold their claim to Kentucky east of the Tennessee River to the British Crown.
Source: [Henderson, Dispelling the Myth: 17th- and 18th-Century Indian Life in Kentucky (Register of the KHS, 1992)](https://preservationkentucky.org/wp-content/uploads/2018/10/Dispelling-the-Myth-17th-18th-Century-Indian-Life-in-KY.pdf)
Source: [1768 Boundary Line Treaty of Fort Stanwix (National Park Service)](https://www.nps.gov/articles/000/1768-boundary-line-treaty-of-fort-stanwix.htm)
